name: Superfiliate
summary: Creator-led growth for D2C brands: run influencer, affiliate and referral programs in one platform across Shopify, Meta and TikTok Shop — discovery, automation, gifting and revenue tracking.
best_for: e-commerce brands turning customers and creators into affiliates with branded co-branded storefronts — if the volume justifies a demo-quoted platform fee
skip_if: you're testing affiliate marketing for the first time — there is no self-serve entry and no published price, so the first step is a sales call about a program that is not yet producing
honest_knock: The price is the part you cannot check. Their pricing page returns 404 with and without www, the homepage carries no figure at all, and the only route to a number is a sales call — so the honest warning is not that it is expensive, but that you cannot compare it against anything until you have spoken to them. Ask for the figure in writing on that call, and ask what separates the ends of whatever range they quote. On fit rather than price: this is built for brands already running creator and affiliate programs, and it is overkill if you are testing your first affiliate offer.

pricing.notes: (read 25 August 2026, re-checked 5 and 24 September 2026) Superfiliate publishes no price on its own site. superfiliate.com/pricing returns 404 with and without www, /llms.txt returns 404, there is no pricing item anywhere in the navigation, and the only commercial call to action is Book Demo. Their Shopify App Store listing (apps.shopify.com/superfiliate) publishes the shape rather than the amount: a single plan named Custom, 'Free to install. Additional charges may apply', the note that the app 'Requires an active Superfiliate subscription for app activation and use. Contact Superfiliate for plan details', and one hard fact — 'All charges are billed in USD.' So the free-to-install label covers the app, not the platform. Our dossier has carried a range of roughly $299 to $999 a month which we cannot trace to their site or to any dated reading; treat it as an unverified order of magnitude rather than a price, and ask for the number in writing on the demo call.

open_questions.question: Can you publish a price, or a starting price, for the plans that are quote-only?
Can a customer cancel at any time, and what happens to an annual plan that is cancelled mid-term?
Which data can a customer export, in which formats, on which plans?
Where is customer data stored, and can a customer choose the region?
Is there a minimum number of seats or users on any plan?
